# Derivation of Lüscher's formula

## Derivation with a simple $\delta$-function potential

# Lüscher's formular in action

## Toy Model

I assume a Hamiltonian with potential of the form

$$
\langle \vec p' | \hat V | \vec p \rangle = V(p',p) = \frac{2\pi C_0}{\mu} f(p') f(p)
$$
$$
f(p) = \exp\left(-\frac{\pi (p r)^2}{32}\right)
$$
$$
C_0^{-1} = \frac{1}{a_0} - \frac{4}{\pi r} \, ,
$$

This is a separable potential with parameters chosen such that

$$
p \cot\delta(p) = \frac{1}{f(p)^2}\left(-\frac{1}{a_0} + \frac{2p}{\sqrt\pi} F\!\left(\tfrac{1}{4} p \sqrt\pi r\right)\right) \approx -\frac{1}{a_0} + \frac{r}{2} p^2 - \frac{r^3}{48} p^4 + \mathcal{O}(p^6)
$$

##

![](assets/fig-toy-pcotdelta.png){fig-align="center" width="95%"}

## Procedure when particles are put in a box

In a box of side length $L$, the eigenenergies $E$ can be obtained by solving the following transcendental equation

$$
-\frac{L}{a_0} + \frac{4L}{\pi r} = \frac{1}{\pi} \sum_{\vec n \in \text{B.Z.}} \frac{f(\vec n)^2}{\vec n^2 - x} \, ,
$$

with $x = \dfrac{m E L^2}{4\pi^2}$ and $f(\vec n) = \exp\left(-\dfrac{\pi^3 r^2}{8 L^2} \vec n^2\right)$. I assume the two particles have equal mass $m$.

Given $x$, I insert this into Lüscher's formula to get the phase shift

$$
p\cot\delta(p) = \frac{1}{\pi L} S(x)
$$

where

$$
S(x) = \lim_{\Lambda \to \infty} \left[ \sum_{\vec n}^{\Lambda} \frac{1}{n^2 - x} - 4\pi\Lambda \right]
$$

## Finite volume dependence of the bound state

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Can be shown that the location of the bound state depends exponentially on $L$

$$
E_{-1}(L) = -\frac{\gamma^2}{m}\left(1 + \frac{12}{\gamma L} \frac{e^{-\gamma L}}{1 - 2\gamma\big(p\cot\delta\big)'} + \dots \right)
$$
$$
\approx -\frac{\gamma^2}{m}\left(1 + \frac{12}{\gamma L} \frac{e^{-\gamma L}}{1 - \gamma r} \right)
$$

Here I define $p = i\gamma$
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](assets/fig-bound-state-L.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}
:::
::::

## Finite volume dependence of lowest scattering state

Lowest scattering state has polynomial dependence on $L$:

$$
E_0(L) = \frac{4\pi a_0}{m L^3}\left(1 + 2.8372974794806 \frac{a_0}{L} + 6.375183165675\left(\frac{a_0}{L}\right)^2 + 8.582925664437\left(\frac{a_0}{L}\right)^3 + 2\pi \frac{a_0^2 r}{L^3} + \dots\right)
$$

Note: $m E_0 = p^2$

![](assets/fig-scattering-state-L.png){fig-align="center" width="55%"}

## Virtual state has same finite volume dependence as a scattering state

Virtual state has polynomial dependence on $L$ just like a regular scattering state:

$$
E_0(L) = \frac{4\pi a_0}{m L^3}\left(1 + 2.8372974794806 \frac{a_0}{L} + 6.375183165675\left(\frac{a_0}{L}\right)^2 + 8.582925664437\left(\frac{a_0}{L}\right)^3 + 2\pi \frac{a_0^2 r}{L^3} + \dots\right)
$$

![](assets/fig-virtual-L-dependence.png){fig-align="center" width="60%"}
